column9: T4L (Technology for Learning) 1:1 program: Chromebooks gr 1-6 (4-6 take-home), iPads in K. District met 1:1 goal in gr 3-6 within ~2 years per 2016 newsletter; specific launch year not pinned.
1:1 Chromebook program K-12: secondary students take home, K-5 assigned Chromebook on classroom carts. Specific launch year not pinned.
District went 1:1 with laptops/Chromebooks during COVID 2020-21 for online learning per state TESR doc. Specific pre-pandemic launch year not documented.
KSD became a 1:1 Chromebook district in grades 2-12 beginning Fall 2020.
One-to-one district issuing Chromebooks to students in grades 3-12. Specific launch year not pinned.
Harvey SD 152 (K-8 elementary district) uses Chromebooks; specific 1:1 launch year not documented.

City Schools of Decatur adopted G Suite for Education in 2015 and Chromebooks in 2016; earlier ~2013 fourth-grade iPad rollout per Google blog (2017). Currently HS/MS take-home Chromebooks; upper elementary cart-based.
Brantley County Schools uses Chromebooks per Instructional Technology page; specific 1:1 launch year not documented.

Major Chromebook distribution effort funded ~$435K in 2020-21 budget; 1,080 laptops distributed to WMS/WHS during COVID. Earlier 2017 funding ($150K) for elementary/middle Chromebooks. Full district 1:1 in 2020.
Dallas County Schools uses Chromebook carts per district website (Content2/Carts page); cart-based use indicates partial rather than 1:1 take-home.
6-12 take-home Chromebooks; 2-5 assigned Chromebooks in classroom; K-1 assigned iPads in classroom. Specific 1:1 launch year not pinned.

Wylie ISD (Taylor County, Abilene) issues Dell Chromebooks to grades 5-12 with take-home for 5-8 and HS via wyliebulldogs.org. Specific launch year not pinned for this Wylie ISD; note this is distinct from Collin Co Wylie ISD whose 2014 pilot/2019 HS rollout is separately documented.
Spartan TecKnow 1:1 initiative provides Chromebooks to grades 4-12 for in-school and at-home use at start of every school year. Specific launch year not pinned (in place by 2021-22).
Rahway 1:1 Chromebook Policy Handbook dated 2019-20 found on district sharpschool. Specific launch year not pinned.

column9: South St. Paul Secondary 1:1 device program standardized on Chromebook for grades 6-12. Specific launch year not pinned.
Appling County Schools Technology Services supports digital learning environment; specific 1:1 Chromebook launch year not documented.
Per Niche student review, Calaveras Unified supplied every student with Chromebooks during COVID, replacing prior shared cart model. Pre-2020 was cart-based (Partial); full 1:1 rollout 2020.

Athens ISD has student device program per district handbooks; specific 1:1 launch year not pinned in available web sources.
2,000 Chromebooks added at elementary and middle schools in 2019; district went fully 1:1 during COVID per ManagedMethods customer story.
HS students receive a laptop, MS has 28 laptop carts, elementary has computer labs and 2 carts each per Great PA Schools profile. Mixed cart/1:1 model; specific 1:1 launch year not pinned.
Hillsboro R-3 has Chromebook program with student handbook and help resources; specific 1:1 launch year not pinned.
BYOD district for grades 5-12; required Chromebook use K-12 starting 2020-21 SY for distance/hybrid learning. District provides Chromebooks via coupon/loaner plan.
USD 450 has Chromebook resources but specific 1:1 launch year not documented in available web sources.
Pike County School District uses Chromebooks; specific 1:1 launch year not documented.
One2World 1:1 device initiative provides each scholar with own device per Summit Technology page. Specific launch year not pinned.
Lee County 1:1 initiative documented on idecorp.com sub-site (1-to-1-chromebook-rollout); Chromebooks distributed within first weeks of school year. Specific launch year not pinned.

1:1 Chromebook initiative; in May 2020 Foundation for Pottstown Education and Pottstown Area Health & Wellness Foundation announced $100K matching grant for Chromebooks during pandemic. District 1:1 in place by 2020.
St. Helens HS does Chromebook checkouts as part of back-to-school activities; district uses Chromebooks 1:1. Specific launch year not pinned.
Durant ISD uses devices but specific 1:1 launch year not documented in available web sources.

Jefferson Township Public School District uses devices; specific 1:1 Chromebook launch year not documented in available web sources.
Carl Junction Schools Chromebook proposal document found (cjr1.org); specific 1:1 launch year not pinned.
Canton 1:1 initiative loans Chromebook laptops to students with computer loan agreement; take-home permitted. Specific launch year not pinned.
Sturgis Public Schools has Chromebook take-home agreement; specific 1:1 launch year not pinned.
Indianola HS students have personal Chromebook through Digital Learning Environment; IT supports 600 staff/3600 students. Specific 1:1 launch year not pinned.

RBUESD K-8 district uses Chromebooks per Technology FAQ page; specific 1:1 launch year not pinned.
Alma School District (Crawford County, AR) - specific 1:1 launch year not documented in available web sources.

Upper Perkiomen SD - specific 1:1 Chromebook launch year not documented in available web sources.
Shippensburg Area SD issues each student a Chromebook at start of school year for content integration and home learning. Specific launch year not pinned.
Wilmington City Schools (OH) launched 1:1 Chromebook initiative at Wilmington High School in 2016-17 SY.
SOCSD began distributing Chromebooks in September 2020 (2020-21 SY); HS had 1:1 program prior per COVID FAQ but specific HS launch year not pinned.
Cornwall Central SD 1:1 Chromebook Initiative launched 2019-2020 school year per district Educational Support page.
Warrensburg R-VI School District - specific 1:1 Chromebook launch year not documented in available web sources.
Sandwich Public Schools provides Chromebooks for all students grades 1-12 with required school-issued device use. Specific 1:1 launch year not pinned.

MSAD 17 (Oxford Hills) participates in Maine Learning Technology Initiative (MLTI), which started fall 2002 providing laptops to all 7th graders statewide; expanded to grade 8 and HS over time. District also has Student Device Guidelines.
Marion County Public Schools (KY) has 1:1 technology in grades 6-12. Specific launch year not pinned.
